41.s: vyuṣṭyāṅgirasakāpivanacaitrarathadvyahānām taṃ te madaṃ gṛṇīmasi iti | dvitīyeṣu viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naram iti |
41.d: व्युष्ट्याङ्गिरसकापिवनचैत्ररथद्व्यहानाम् तं ते मदं गृणीमसि इति । द्वितीयेषु विश्वाः पृतना अभिभूतरं नरम् इति ।
41.m: In the two-day rites of the Vyuṣṭi, the Āṅgirasa, the Kāpivana, [and] the Caitraratha: “That exhilaration of thine we celebrate”; on the second days: “The man overcoming all hostile armies”.

41.s: cāturmāsyavaiśvadevagargabaidacchandomavatparākāntarvasvaśvamedhatryahāṇāṃ śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate iti |
41.d: चातुर्मास्यवैश्वदेवगर्गबैदच्छन्दोमवत्पराकान्तर्वस्वश्वमेधत्र्यहाणां शग्ध्य् ऊ षु शचीपते इति ।
41.m: In the three-day rites of the Cāturmāsya, the Vaiśvadeva, the Garga, the Baida, the Chandomavat, the Parāka, the Antarvasu, [and] the Aśvamedha: “Be capable, O lord of power”.

41.s: sākamedhasya indram id devatātaye iti |
41.d: साकमेधस्य इन्द्रम् इद् देवतातये इति ।
41.m: In that of the Sākamedha: “Indra indeed for the worship of the gods”.

41.s: baidasvarasāmnoḥ tvaṃ na indrā bhara iti |
41.d: बैदस्वरसाम्नोः त्वं न इन्द्रा भर इति ।
41.m: In the Baida and the Svarasāman: “Bring to us, O Indra”.

41.s: dvitīyeṣu tam indraṃ vājayāmasi astāvi manma pūrvyam taṃ te madaṃ gṛṇīmasi iti |
41.d: द्वितीयेषु तम् इन्द्रं वाजयामसि अस्तावि मन्म पूर्व्यम् तं ते मदं गृणीमसि इति ।
41.m: On the second days: “We urge that Indra to battle”, “The ancient thought has been praised”, [and] “That exhilaration of thine we celebrate”.

41.s: aśvamedhasya vācam aṣṭāpadīm aham svādor itthā viṣūvataḥ iti |
41.d: अश्वमेधस्य वाचम् अष्टापदीम् अहम् स्वादोर् इत्था विषूवतः इति ।
41.m: In that of the Horse Sacrifice: “An eight-footed speech I”, [and] “The sweet [draught] thus of the Viṣūvant”.

41.s: pṛṣṭhyatryahasya evā hy asi vīrayuḥ ity ukthe |
41.d: पृष्ठ्यत्र्यहस्य एवा ह्य् असि वीरयुः इत्य् उक्थे ।
41.m: In the Pṛṣṭhya three-day rite, in the uktha: “For thus art thou desirous of heroes”.

41.s: tṛtīyeṣu mahā;m indro ya ojasā abhi pra vaḥ surādhasam evā hy asi vīrayuḥ iti |
41.d: तृतीयेषु महा;म् इन्द्रो य ओजसा अभि प्र वः सुराधसम् एवा ह्य् असि वीरयुः इति ।
41.m: On the third days: “Great is Indra who through might”, “Forth to your bountiful one”, [and] “For thus art thou desirous of heroes”.

41.s: sākamedhasya tam indraṃ vājayāmasi śrāyanta iva sūryam iti |
41.d: साकमेधस्य तम् इन्द्रं वाजयामसि श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् इति ।
41.m: In that of the Sākamedha: “We urge that Indra to battle” [and] “Like those taking refuge in the sun”.

41.s: caturahāṇāṃ śrāyanta iva sūryam tvaṃ na indrā bhara iti |
41.d: चतुरहाणां श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् त्वं न इन्द्रा भर इति ।
41.m: In the four-day rites: “Like those taking refuge in the sun” [and] “Bring to us, O Indra”.

41.s: caturtheṣu mahā;m indro ya ojasā ya eka id vidayate iti |
41.d: चतुर्थेषु महा;म् इन्द्रो य ओजसा य एक इद् विदयते इति ।
41.m: On the fourth days: “Great is Indra who through might” [and] “He who alone distributes”.

41.s: sarveṣu mā bhūma niṣṭyā iva vidhuṃ dadrāṇaṃ salilasya pṛṣṭhe iti |
41.d: सर्वेषु मा भूम निष्ट्या इव विधुं दद्राणं सलिलस्य पृष्ठे इति ।
41.m: In all of them: “May we not be like strangers” [and] “The moon running on the surface of the waters”.

41.s: saṃsarpacaturvīrayoḥ ayam u te samatasi imā u tvā purūvaso iti |
41.d: संसर्पचतुर्वीरयोः अयम् उ ते समतसि इमा उ त्वा पुरूवसो इति ।
41.m: In the Saṃsarpa and Caturvīra: “And this roaming of thine” [and] “These unto thee, O lord of much wealth”.

41.s: pañcāheṣu trivṛdādivat |
41.d: पञ्चाहेषु त्रिवृदादिवत् ।
41.m: In the five-day rites: as in the Trivṛt and so forth.

41.s: abhyāsaṅgyapañcaśāradīyayor dvitīye tvaṃ na indrā bhara iti |
41.d: अभ्यासङ्ग्यपञ्चशारदीययोर् द्वितीये त्वं न इन्द्रा भर इति ।
41.m: On the second [day] of the Abhyāsaṅgya and the Pañcaśāradīya: “Bring to us, O Indra”.

41.s: pṛṣṭhyapañcāhasya evā hy asi vīrayuḥ iti |
41.d: पृष्ठ्यपञ्चाहस्य एवा ह्य् असि वीरयुः इति ।
41.m: In the Pṛṣṭhya five-day rite: “For thus art thou desirous of heroes”.

41.s: pañcame uttiṣṭhann ojasā saha indro madāya vāvṛdhe indrāya sāma gāyata iti |
41.d: पञ्चमे उत्तिष्ठन्न् ओजसा सह इन्द्रो मदाय वावृधे इन्द्राय साम गायत इति ।
41.m: On the fifth: “Arising together with might”, “Indra has grown for exhilaration”, [and] “Sing a sāman to Indra”.

41.s: abhiplavapañcāhasya ya eka id vidayate iti |
41.d: अभिप्लवपञ्चाहस्य य एक इद् विदयते इति ।
41.m: In the Abhiplava five-day rite: “He who alone distributes”.

41.s: abhyāsaṅgyapañcaśāradīyayoḥ śrāyanta iva sūryam iti |
41.d: अभ्यासङ्ग्यपञ्चशारदीययोः श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् इति ।
41.m: In the Abhyāsaṅgya and the Pañcaśāradīya: “Like those taking refuge in the sun”.

41.s: ṣaḍahasya gavi abhrātṛvyo anā tvam iti | āyuṣi tvaṃ na indrā bhara iti |
41.d: षडहस्य गवि अभ्रातृव्यो अना त्वम् इति । आयुषि त्वं न इन्द्रा भर इति ।
41.m: In the Go day of the six-day rite: “Without a rival indeed art thou”; in the Āyus day: “Bring to us, O Indra”.

41.s: pañcame endra no gadhi priyaḥ iti |
41.d: पञ्चमे एन्द्र नो गधि प्रियः इति ।
41.m: On the fifth: “Come to us, dear one”.

41.s: ṣaṣṭham ukthyaṃ cet ya eka id vidayate yat somam indra viṣṇavi iti |
41.d: षष्ठम् उक्थ्यं चेत् य एक इद् विदयते यत् सोमम् इन्द्र विष्णवि इति ।
41.m: If the sixth is an ukthya: “He who alone distributes” [and] “The soma which, O Indra, at Viṣṇu's”.

42.s: pṛṣṭhasya dvitīye evā hy asi vīrayuḥ iti |
42.d: पृष्ठस्य द्वितीये एवा ह्य् असि वीरयुः इति ।
42.m: On the second [day] of the Pṛṣṭha: “For thus art thou desirous of heroes”.

42.s: tṛtīye indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ tvaṃ na indrā bhara iti |
42.d: तृतीये इन्द्रेण सं हि दृक्षसे वयं घ त्वा सुतावन्तः त्वं न इन्द्रा भर इति ।
42.m: On the third: “For thou art seen together with Indra”, “We indeed who have pressed the soma for thee”, [and] “Bring to us, O Indra”.

42.s: daśāhasyāṣṭame yad indra prāg apāg udak iti |
42.d: दशाहस्याष्टमे यद् इन्द्र प्राग् अपाग् उदक् इति ।
42.m: On the eighth [day] of the ten-day rite: “If, O Indra, east, west, north”.

42.s: navame eto nv indraṃ stavāma iti |
42.d: नवमे एतो न्व् इन्द्रं स्तवाम इति ।
42.m: On the ninth: “Come now, let us praise Indra”.

42.s: trikakuddaśāhasya navasu śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate abhi pra gopatiṃ girā taṃ vo dasmam ṛtīṣaham vayam enam idā hyaḥ indram id gāthino bṛhat śrāyanta iva sūryam ka īṃ veda sute sacā viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naram yad indra prāg apāg udak iti |
42.d: त्रिककुद्दशाहस्य नवसु शग्ध्य् ऊ षु शचीपते अभि प्र गोपतिं गिरा तं वो दस्मम् ऋतीषहम् वयम् एनम् इदा ह्यः इन्द्रम् इद् गाथिनो बृहत् श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् क ईं वेद सुते सचा विश्वाः पृतना अभिभूतरं नरम् यद् इन्द्र प्राग् अपाग् उदक् इति ।
42.m: For the nine [days] of the Trikakud Daśāha, [the verses are]: "Help well, O lord of power", "Sing forth to the lord of the cow with verse", "To that accomplished one of yours, who overcomes attacks", "We [invoke] him now, yesterday", "Singers [magnify] Indra greatly", "As if clinging to the sun", "Who knows him when the soma is pressed?", "The man who overcomes all armies", [and] "Whether, O Indra, from the east, west, or north".

42.s: aṣṭame mahā;m indro ya ojasā iti |
42.d: अष्टमे महा;म् इन्द्रो य ओजसा इति ।
42.m: On the eighth [day]: "Indra is great, who by his might".

42.s: dvādaśāhasya chandomaprathamāntyayoḥ tvaṃ na indrā bhara ya eka id vidayate iti |
42.d: द्वादशाहस्य छन्दोमप्रथमान्त्ययोः त्वं न इन्द्रा भर य एक इद् विदयते इति ।
42.m: On the first and last of the Chandoma [days] of the Twelve-Day Rite: "Bring to us, O Indra", [and] "He who alone distributes".

42.s: svarasāmasu saṃ codaya citram arvāk praṇetāraṃ vasyo acchā iti paryāyeṇa | abhiplave ca |
42.d: स्वरसामसु सं चोदय चित्रम् अर्वाक् प्रणेतारं वस्यो अच्छा इति पर्यायेण । अभिप्लवे च ।
42.m: At the Svarasāman [days]: "Impel hither the wondrous [wealth]", [and] "To the guide towards better things" alternately; and also at the Abhiplava.

42.s: tanūpṛṣṭhe abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ tvām id dhi havāmahe yad dyāva indra te śatam pibā somam indra mandatu tvā kayā naś citra ā bhuvat revatīr naḥ sadhamāde iti |
42.d: तनूपृष्ठे अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमः त्वाम् इद् धि हवामहे यद् द्याव इन्द्र ते शतम् पिबा सोमम् इन्द्र मन्दतु त्वा कया नश् चित्र आ भुवत् रेवतीर् नः सधमादे इति ।
42.m: In the case of Tanūpṛṣṭha: "Unto thee, hero, we shout", "Thee indeed we call upon", "If, O Indra, a hundred heavens were thine", "Drink soma, O Indra; let it intoxicate thee", "By what wondrous [aid] will he be present to us?", [and] "Rich ones, with us in festive gathering".

42.d: एतेषाम् अनन्तरो ऽनुरूपः संभवे । स्तोत्रियनियमश् छन्दसा ।
42.m: The antistrophe verse immediately follows these, when possible; the rule for the strophe verse is according to the meter.
By the Gavāmayana, the year-long [sacrifices] are explained.

42.s: etasmād evāhīnā rātrisattrāṇi | ekāhā api kecit |
42.d: एतस्माद् एवाहीना रात्रिसत्त्राणि । एकाहा अपि केचित् ।
42.m: From this very [model] come the ahīna sacrifices, the night sessions, and also certain one-day rites.
Everywhere the arrangement of wishes is according to the Sāmaveda.

42.d: द्व्यहप्रभृतयो ऽहीना आ द्वादशाहात् । अन्यतरतो ऽतिरात्रात् ।
42.m: Ahīna sacrifices range from two-day rites up to the twelve-day rite, [characterized] by an Atirātra at either end.
Night sessions range from twelve days up to short of a year.
The ten-night rite has an Atirātra at both ends.
The twelve-day rite with an Agniṣṭoma first is an ahīna sacrifice.
Sacrificial courses extend up to a thousand years; one should sacrifice with a Viśvajit as an equivalent to a thousand-year sacrifice.

43.s: agnyādheyaṃ vasante brāhmaṇasya brahmavarcasakāmasya | grīṣme rājanyasya tejaskāmasya | varṣāsu vaiśyasya puṣṭikāmasya | śaradi sarveṣāṃ gadāpanuttaye |
43.d: अग्न्याधेयं वसन्ते ब्राह्मणस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य । ग्रीष्मे राजन्यस्य तेजस्कामस्य । वर्षासु वैश्यस्य पुष्टिकामस्य । शरदि सर्वेषां गदापनुत्तये ।
43.m: The setting up of the sacred fires [is performed] in spring for a brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual lustre, in summer for a kṣatriya desiring vigor, in the rainy season for a vaiśya desiring prosperity, [and] in autumn for all to ward off disease.
According to some, it concludes with the full-spoon offering.
For those who perform the Agnihotra, [it extends to that point], according to the young Kauśika.
For them, at the first-fruits offering, [an offering] of new grain [is made].
The Agnihotra [is performed] with a boiled rice offering or with barley gruel.

43.s: abhāve gavīḍāṃ navaghāsam āśayitvā tasyāḥ payasā |
43.d: अभावे गवीडां नवघासम् आशयित्वा तस्याः पयसा ।
43.m: In the absence [of these], having fed the cow fresh grass, with her milk.
For one desiring prosperity, there is constant keeping awake of the fires.
The Agnihotra is for one desiring heaven.
With rice grains, for one desiring strength.
With soma, for one desiring spiritual lustre.
The New and Full Moon sacrifices are for one desiring all wishes.
The Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice is for one desiring offspring.
The Sākaṃprasthāyya sacrifice is for one desiring cattle.
The Saṃkrama sacrifice is for one desiring all wishes.
The Iḍādadha is for one desiring cattle.
The Sārvasena sacrifice is for one desiring offspring.
The Śaunaka sacrifice is for one desiring a malevolent rite.
The Vasiṣṭha sacrifice is for one desiring offspring.
The course of Heaven and Earth is for one desiring firm standing.
These are the sacrificial courses of the New and Full Moon sacrifices.
The first-fruits offering is for one desiring food.
The four-month sacrifices are for one desiring all wishes.
The animal [sacrifice] to Indra and Agni is for one desiring life, offspring, and cattle.

43.s: yāmaḥ śukahariḥ śuṇṭho vānāmayakāmasya pitṛlokakāmasya ca |
43.d: यामः शुकहरिः शुण्ठो वानामयकामस्य पितृलोककामस्य च ।
43.m: A white-yellowish or gelded animal sacred to Yama is for one desiring freedom from disease and for one desiring the realm of the ancestors.
A mare sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ is for one desiring offspring.
The Vājapeya is for one desiring sovereign rule.
The Atirātra is for one desiring prosperity.
The Gavāmayana and the twelve-day rite [are likewise].
The Rājasūya is for one desiring sovereign rule.
The Horse Sacrifice and Human Sacrifice are for one desiring all wishes.
The Universal Sacrifice is for one desiring preeminence.
Because desires are endless, sacrifices are limitless.
They are explained by their archetype sacrifices.
The order of sacrifice is [known] from the Brāhmaṇa, as is the repairing of defects.

43.s: ya imau kalpāv adhīte ya u caivaṃ veda tena sarvaiḥ kratubhir iṣṭaṃ bhavati sarvāṃś ca kāmān āpnoti |
43.d: य इमौ कल्पाव् अधीते य उ चैवं वेद तेन सर्वैः क्रतुभिर् इष्टं भवति सर्वांश् च कामान् आप्नोति ।
43.m: Whoever studies these two ritual procedures and whoever knows thus—by him sacrifice has been made with all sacrifices, and he attains all desires.

43.s: athāpy udāharanti yathā yaṣṭus tathādhyetur eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir iti |
43.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति यथा यष्टुस् तथाध्येतुर् एषा ब्राह्मी प्रतिश्रुतिर् एषा ब्राह्मी प्रतिश्रुतिर् इति ।
43.m: Now also they quote: “As for the sacrificer, so for the reciter; this is the echo of the brahman, this is the echo of the brahman.”
